newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece can join EMU by end-2001 - cenbank governor.
newsitem.headline: Greece can join EMU by end-2001 - cenbank governor.

text.p: Greece will be able to join EMU by the end of 2001 provided the right mix of economic policy and the necessary structural reforms are implemented, said Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos.

"To the extent that the proper macroeconomic policy is implemented ...and the necessary structural reforms are being pushed forward, the country can join EMU by 2001 and combine it with rising real incomes," said Papademos.
He was speaking to a conference on the Greek economy organised by the Economist business magazine.
The simultaneous achievement of monetary stability and development depends to a large extent on the mix of economic policy and especially the degree of fiscal adjustment, he said.
Inflation has been falling rapidly since the beginning of the year, reflecting the effects of a stable foreign exchange and restrictive monetary policy with a time lag, he added.

The reversal of the negative effects of higher international petrol and fresh fruit and vegetables prices on 1996 inflation, coupled with the continued hard drachma policy explain the recent drop in inflation, said Papademos.
Greek CPI-based inflation fell to 6.0 percent year-on-year in March from 6.6 percent in February.
"It is encouraging that core inflation which is affected by internal factors is experiencing a corresponding deceleration in the beginning of 1997," he said.
The anticipated slowdown in the increase of unit labour costs and consistent implementation of fiscal policy will contribute to the deceleration of inflation in 1997 and 1998, said Papademos.
"Therefore, the conditions favour the de-escalation of inflation to levels below 3.0 percent in 1998, that will approach the relative convergence criterion," he said.
Bank of Greece has said it targets an inflation rate of 4.5 percent at end-1997 and below 3.0 percent by end 1998. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Intercontinental Newsroom +301 3311813
